page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine configured with 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel x86_64 cores using hyper-threading. The system allocates 32 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4 GB per virtual core. Its processor architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache, alongside instruction support for AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix acceleration. The instance does not include local disk storage or GPU accelerators, necessitating network-attached storage for operating system and data volumes.

Benchmark results place the instance primarily within the middle 50% performance bracket. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng evaluations yielded 1676.09 and 6902.54 respectively, complemented by a Geekbench multi-core score of 6838.0. Network and operational throughput demonstrate steady mid-tier capability, sustaining 12.95 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks and 9.71 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, memory-intensive operations showed vulnerabilities: multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark memory testing registered in the bottom 25% of tested configurations.

The qualitative efficiency of the n4-standard-8 stems from dedicated CPU core allocation, which avoids noisy-neighbor throttling typical of shared-core options. While compute and cache capabilities handle standard multi-threaded tasks effectively, the platform is ill-suited for hardware-accelerated tasks, evidenced by poor 7B model LLM text generation at 6.31 tokens per second. The instance is appropriate for web serving tiers, software compilation using Clang, Redis caching layers, and microservices workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-8 is a balanced general-purpose virtual machine providing 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical Intel x86_64 cores and 32 GB of RAM. The instance incorporates modern vector and matrix extensions including AVX-512 and AMX, backed by 260 MB of L3 cache. It contains no local NVMe storage and zero GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached block volumes. Benchmark testing shows consistent mid-tier performance across Geekbench compute, clang compilation, and Redis throughput with 9.71 million operations per second. However, synthetic memory metrics and multi-threaded decompression fall into the lower quartile, and large language model inference shows poor throughput due to the absence of dedicated accelerators. The configuration delivers predictable compute performance suitable for static web serving, containerized enterprise microservices, build pipelines, and mid-tier caching layers.
